newsitem.title: RWANDA: Rwanda closes Red Cross centre for refugees.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda closes Red Cross centre for refugees.

text.p: Rwanda on Monday closed a Red Cross centre for sick and exhausted Rwandan refugees near its border, forcing the tens of thousands of people returning from Zaire to trek deeper into their homeland.
A Red Cross spokesman said two men who identified themselves as from the ministry of rehabilitation ordered the centre at Umbano camp in the border town of Gisenyi closed immediately.
Thirty minutes later they returned with trucks to the centre, which had only been established on Monday, said Andrew Hall of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.
"They didn't give specific reasons, only that they wanted the camps around the borders moved," said Hall, adding 350 sick and exhausted refugees were put on trucks and driven away.
It was the most public clash between aid agencies and the Rwandan authorities since refugees started flooding over the border from Zaire and towards their homes on Friday.
The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) estimated 500,000 Rwandan refugees had crossed but noted the flood had dried to a trickle on Monday.

At Nkamira town an estimated 10,000 refugees thronged the streets, having walked for up to four days from Zaire to reach what the UNHCR had promoted as the first major transit centre where they could eat and rest on the way home.
The only Hutu refugees allowed into the transit centre, a large walled compound funded and built by UNHCR and other aid agencies, were parents looking for lost children.

The only traffic in and out of the compound were trucks to carry refugees to their home districts and other trucks carrying some of the 2,000 children who have been separated from their parents on the march.
On the main road outside the gate, refugees fought in a chaotic scramble to board trucks from the UNHCR and the International Organisation for Migration (IOM).

At the back of one truck, guards wielding sticks pushed back people fighting to board the already crammed vehicle. A baby fell from the truck into the road while another was thrown into the back of the vehicle by an anguished young mother separated from her husband in the crush.

Aid workers, who declined to be identified, accuse Rwandan authorities of tying up aid agencies in bureaucracy to block food distribution to the refugees in an attempt to force them to keep moving away from Rwanda's border with Zaire.

"There was no physical violence. Sticks were waved around but they weren't used," Hall told a news conference after the centre was closed, adding the International Federation of Red Coss and Red Crescent Societies had made representations to the govenment.

He said Rwandan officials told the Red Cross the 350, including mothers with newly born babies, elderly, disabled and people in "fairly unstable medical condition", were being taken to a U.N. centre at Nkamira, 21 km (13 miles) northeast of Gisenyi.
Hall said the Red Cross was concerned at their condition, noting a woman, with a child, had died at the centre before the closure.

Aid workers said many Hutu refugees were so scared of the Tutsi-dominated army that the presence of a single guard at the entrance and other soldiers along the road had stopped them using the transit centre.
UNHCR spokesman Mans Nyberg said he hoped the camp would reopen: "It should be operating as the transit centre which it was designed to be where people can rest, get food and stay overnight."
